summary: The patch wires up the previously-ignored tzinfo, but resolves the zone name via self.tzinfo.tzname(None), which is a fragile approach that diverges from the project's existing get_tzname() helper. For common tzinfo types this yields an abbreviation/LMT/None rather than the IANA zone name, producing wrong or no-op results outside the narrow case exercised by the test.

issues.description: self.tzinfo.tzname(None) is the wrong abstraction for deriving a DB timezone name. tzname() is DST/datetime-dependent: for a pytz zone the un-localized instance returns a stale abbreviation/LMT, for zoneinfo.ZoneInfo it returns None (so the conversion is silently skipped and the bug is NOT fixed), and for a fixed-offset datetime.timezone it returns 'UTC-05:00'-style strings that are not valid DB timezone identifiers. Passing an abbreviation like 'EST' to AT TIME ZONE drops DST handling and gives incorrect dates for half the year. Django already has the TimeZone mixin's get_tzname()/timezone._g

Incomplete: the inline branch does not handle a tzinfo passed as a string and does not work for zoneinfo-based timezones (tzname(None) -> None), so the stated goal ('pass in any tzinfo / America_New_York while app is UTC') is only met for the specific timezone object type used by the repro test.

Logic is duplicated inline in two as_sql() methods as a dense nested ternary rather than reusing the existing get_tzname() helper, hurting readability and risking divergence between TruncDate/TruncTime and the rest of the TimeZone mixin.
